text:
The Maple Leafs won on Monday for the first time since Halloween, 4-2 on Long Island, with rookie Gavin McKenna scoring the go-ahead goal on a delayed penalty, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner. It ended a nine-game winless run that produced a season's worth of noise in two weeks.

"We should be embarrassed," Auston Matthews said during the skid, as The Times of India headlined it, and Elliotte Friedman said of Matthews' future, "All bets are off," per The Hockey Beast. Coach Jim Hiller has called out William Nylander's costly mistakes, per Yahoo Sports, and trade columns now cover both stars. Former coach Bruce Boudreau has criticised Hiller's handling of McKenna, and Chris Tanev pushed back on his own load management.

The numbers say the record is close to fair. Toronto is 9-14-3 with 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our standings model has it about four points behind its play. Sergei Bobrovsky is part of that gap: 0-5-0 over his last five starts with an .827 save rate, 7.6 goals worse than expected. Nylander has 4 points in his last 10 games against 9.9 expected.

The line that works is Matthews with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan, 11 goals for and 4 against at 5-on-5. Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh get 46% of the chances. Our playoff odds are 3%. What we'd watch: whether one win changes any of the conversations, starting with Matthews.
headline: One win ends the skid, not the questions
